subject: Preflight: workload census & session-affinity details for VertexHealth Dedicated
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah@vertexhealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Jul 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Preflight: workload census & session-affinity details for VertexHealth Dedicated

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for taking this on. To scope a Dedicated footprint that meets VertexHealth's latency and SLA goals we need a quick, focused census of your traffic profile. I've attached the Redwood pre-sales workbook (redwood_pre_sales_workbook_v1.xlsx) with a small CSV template; filling the CSV is fastest but a short reply with the key numbers below works too.

Please provide (ballpark is fine):
- Peak sustained QPS (30m) and absolute 5m peak QPS
- Peak concurrent sessions and percent of requests that are stateful sessions (KV cache / streaming chat) vs stateless completions
- Typical prompt token distribution (pct <50, 50–200, 200–1000) and median prompt tokens
- Typical response token distribution and median response tokens
- Percent of requests using streaming vs non-streaming responses
- Target p95 end-to-end latency (ms) and SLO tier for this deal (e.g., p50<120ms, p95<350ms)
- Percent of traffic that tolerates degraded model quality (fallback to quantized model) vs must always use highest-quality variant
- Session duration (avg and 95th) and sticky-session fraction (sessions pinned to a GPU / cache)
- Any predicted dayparting (UTC ranges with >2x baseline) and planned traffic growth for next 12 months

Also: are you planning any large nightly batch jobs or embeddings-heavy workloads that would share the same Dedicated pool? If so, note typical batch QPS and window.

Next steps after you send numbers: we run a short sizing hypothesis, identify candidate GPU SKU mix (including quantized variants), and propose a pilot canary (2–3 nodes) to run a 24h replay.

Thanks — if easier, send the CSV sample and I can pull numbers in.

Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: redwood_pre_sales_workbook_v1.xlsx (workbook with sample traffic CSV template, fields: timestamp,qps,concurrency,prompt_tokens,response_tokens,streaming_flag,session_id)
From: Sarah Park <sarah@vertexhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@vertexhealth.com
Date: Fri, 22 Jul 2028 12:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Preflight: workload census & session-affinity details for VertexHealth Dedicated

Jonas —

Appreciate the checklist. I've attached a small sample (vertex_sample_traffic.csv) pulled from last week's production window — it's anonymized and representative of peak behaviour. High-level summary below (ballpark):

- Peak 5m QPS: 450 
- Peak sustained 30m QPS: 290
- Peak concurrent sessions: ~320 active sessions
- Stateful sessions (chat with KV cache): ~58% of traffic (these maintain short-term context per user)
- Prompt token distribution: ~50% <50 tokens, 38% 50–200, 12% 200–1000; median prompt tokens ~42
- Response tokens: median ~280, 90th percentile ~820
- Streaming usage: ~65% of chat flows prefer streaming (progressive render)
- Target SLO: p95 end-to-end ~350ms (we'd like p50 ~120ms)
- Quality constraints: 75% of requests can tolerate q4_0 quantized fallback for cost reasons; 25% require fp16/high-quality model (HIPAA-sensitive flows)
- Avg session duration: 3m (95th ~18m); sticky session fraction: ~72% (we prefer session affinity to preserve cache warm state)
- Dayparting: notable spike 16:00–20:00 PT (approx +2.2x baseline) Mon–Fri

We do have nightly batch summarization jobs that run in a 02:00–04:00 PT window; they are embeddings-heavy but low-concurrency (background: ~20 qps).

Questions for you:
1) How does Redwood model warm-kv cache sizing — do you provision extra RAM per GPU or an external KV tier?
2) What's the recommended guardrail for burst > peak (we anticipate marketing-driven surges up to ~3x for 10–15 minute campaigns)?

Thanks — attaching vertex_sample_traffic.csv. Happy to jump on a quick call if that helps.

—Sarah Park
VP Product, VertexHealth
Sarah.Park@vertexhealth.com
Attachment: vertex_sample_traffic.csv (sample rows, header: timestamp,qps,concurrency,prompt_tokens,response_tokens,streaming_flag,session_id)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah@vertexhealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Jul 2028 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Preflight: workload census & session-affinity details for VertexHealth Dedicated

Sarah —

This is excellent, thanks for the quick turnaround and the sample CSV — that lets us move from hypothesis to concrete sizing. Quick notes and next steps below:

Summary of what I heard (confirm if I missed anything):
- Peak 5m QPS: 450, sustained 30m: 290, peak concurrent ~320
- ~58% stateful (KV-backed chat), sticky sessions ~72%
- Median prompt ~42 tokens, median response ~280 tokens, streaming used ~65%
- Dayparting 16:00–20:00 PT ~+2.2x baseline, occasional marketing surges up to ~3x for short bursts
- 75% of traffic acceptable to fall back to q4_0; 25% must use higher-quality model (fp16) due to compliance-sensitive content

Sizing implications (initial hypothesis):
- Pilot cluster: 3 x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs (or similar high-memory SKUs) to run a replay and validate tiling/occupancy assumptions; pilot will exercise sticky-session paths + streaming.
- Production Dedicated baseline: a blended pool with lane separation:
  - 6–8 quantized GPU instances for cost-sensitive traffic (q4_0) with autoscale headroom for 2x bursts
  - 2–3 fp16 GPUs reserved for high-quality lanes and to serve as immediate fallback during degraded quantized performance
- KV cache strategy: we recommend colocated in-GPU KV for fastest hot-path (keeps p95 low). For larger working sets we suggest a small external in-memory tier (Redis with local hot cache) to avoid GPU memory fragmentation. Camila, can you run a quick sim of cache hit-rates at 72% stickiness and 50k active keys?

Burst handling & guardrails:
- For marketing-style 10–15m 3x spikes we recommend a short-lived burst pool (burst credits) that auto-enables an extra 20–30% GPU cushion plus cross-region fallback to maintain p95 while autoscale stabilizes.
- Canary approach: launch pilot, run 24h replay, then a staged ramp to 25%/50%/100% traffic over three days.

Questions I have for you (to finalize proposal):
- Can you identify the 25% of traffic that must never fall back? Are those user cohorts / API routes / endpoints we can tag?
- Any constraints on cross-region failover? (e.g., data residency / latency limits)

Next steps (proposed):
1) Camila runs cache-impact sim and confirms GPU memory delta (assigned).
2) Marissa to prepare a Dedicated pricing sketch (baseline + burst credits + pilot pricing).
3) I will schedule a 30-min infra sync early next week to review the 24h replay plan and pilot cluster sizing.

I'll attach a quick capacity sketch (capacity_sketch_v1.pdf) and follow up with the pilot run playbook once Camila's sim is in.

If that plan looks good I'll set the infra sync and send a calendar invite.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
Attachment: capacity_sketch_v1.pdf (one-page sketch: pilot cluster + prod lane split + burst pool)
